items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: It was released in England by my great friend Doug Dobell,

ctx.x: Buddy Tate had been in Paris and in Europe for a concert tour. I asked him if he would be interested to make a record with me for Pathe-Marconi. He liked very much the idea but had difficulties with the manager who had brought him in Europe. Jean-Marie Monnestier who was against the idea. He told Buddy that if he made the record, Monnestier would not pay his fare back to the U.S.A. So until the last minute, we still did not know if he would be there for the recording. The studio had been hired, so were the…

I did another recording for a British fellow who was trying to push a young British pianist named Mike Garret. I was told that Mike had been doing a lot of classical piano, was very talented and wanted to play jazz. We decided to record in Paris with Art Taylor on drums, Jean Francois Castoire on bass and Francois Guin, named "Frick" on trombone. We found out that Mike had never before played with an ensemble and didn't know the art of accompanying soloists. We did our best and called the album "Three Generations…

The same routine went on during most of 1969. Concert tour in Switzerland with the New Ragtime Band directed by a very sensitive clarinet player, Jacky Millet. Concerts in France, with my group with Marc Hemmler, piano, Pierre Sim, bass, and Francho Manzzechi on drums. I was giving now and then, Negro Spirituals concerts. I was part of a show with a big choral from Lyon, "the Bardanes".
